title: Cost Optimization pillar (avoid unnecessary spend)
hook: Cost Optimization means delivering business value at the lowest price point — not cheapest at the expense of reliability. Continuously monitor, attribute, and eliminate waste while rightsizing for actual demand.

blocks.text: Principles: implement cloud financial management, adopt consumption models, measure overall efficiency, stop spending on undifferentiated heavy lifting, and analyze and attribute expenditure. Tools: Cost Explorer, Budgets, CUR (Cost and Usage Report), Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, Graviton instances.

entries.plainDefinition: Detailed billing line items for analysis
entries.example: Athena query on S3 CUR parquet

entries.plainDefinition: Allocate spend to teams via tags

blocks.text: FinOps is a senior interview theme: "how do you know which team spent what?" and "how do you reduce NAT Gateway data processing charges?" Cost pillar conflicts with Reliability — articulate the tradeoff.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: tag everything, budgets/alarms, right-size, Savings Plans/RI, eliminate waste, unit economics.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Tag and allocate
items.body: Mandatory tags: environment, cost-center, workload. SCP enforce tag-on-create.

items.title: Monitor and budget
items.body: AWS Budgets with alerts at 80/100% forecast.

items.title: Right-size and purchase
items.body: Compute Optimizer + Savings Plans for steady baseline.

items.title: Eliminate waste
items.body: Idle EIPs, unattached EBS, old snapshots, over-provisioned NAT.

diagram.title: FinOps loop
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  TAG[Tag resources] --> MON[Cost Explorer]
  MON --> BUD[Budgets alarm]
  BUD --> ACT[Right-size / SP]
  ACT --> TAG

snippet.label: Cost Explorer by tag
snippet.code:
aws ce get-cost-and-usage \
  --time-period Start=2026-01-01,End=2026-02-01 \
  --granularity MONTHLY \
  --metrics UnblendedCost \
  --group-by Type=TAG,Key=cost-center
snippet.explanation: Showback per team — foundation of cost governance.

snippet.label: Budget alert
snippet.code:
MonthlyBudget:
  Type: AWS::Budgets::Budget
  Properties:
    Budget:
      BudgetName: prod-monthly
      BudgetLimit:
        Amount: 50000
        Unit: USD
      TimeUnit: MONTHLY
    NotificationsWithSubscribers:
      - Notification:
          Threshold: 80
          ComparisonOperator: GREATER_THAN
        Subscribers:
          - SubscriptionType: EMAIL
            Address: finops@example.com

snippet.label: Athena CUR — top NAT cost
snippet.code:
SELECT line_item_resource_id, SUM(line_item_unblended_cost) AS cost
FROM cur_db.cur_table
WHERE product_product_name = 'Amazon VPC'
  AND line_item_usage_type LIKE '%NatGateway%'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10;
snippet.explanation: NAT data processing often surprises — query CUR for proof.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: No tagging — cannot allocate spend. Buying 3-year RIs for experimental workloads. Ignoring data transfer and NAT Gateway costs.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: unit cost dashboard ($/request); month-over-month waste reduction; Savings Plan coverage %; budget forecast accuracy.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying "serverless is always cheaper" — rejected. Strong answer: match pricing model to traffic pattern; measure unit economics.

interviewTakeaways: Cost Optimization = visibility, allocation, right-size, commitment discounts, eliminate waste.
Tagging is prerequisite — untagged spend is ungovernable.
NAT Gateway and data transfer are silent cost drivers.
60s: Tag, Budgets, Cost Explorer, CUR/Athena, right-size, Savings Plans for steady load, eliminate idle resources. Unit economics over raw bill.
Follow-up: Cost vs Reliability — when is single NAT OK?
commonPitfalls: No tags on prod resources — cannot answer "who spent this?"
Strong answer: mandatory tags, SCP enforcement, showback dashboards.

jsTsCorrelations.note: More Lambda memory = more CPU and cost — tune with Power Tuning tool, not max memory.
Smaller esbuild bundles reduce Lambda GB-seconds — cost and performance link.
